summary: Defines a YANG data model for Large-Scale Measurement Platform Measurement Agents. It provides a machine-readable way to describe their configuration and reporting.

eli5.summary: A fill-in form, in a computer-friendly format, for describing measuring gadgets.

questions: what is the lmap yang model
subtitle: A machine-readable YANG description of how measurement agents are configured, scheduled and report results.

tldr.problem: Large-scale measurement platforms need a standard, machine-readable way to tell Measurement Agents what to measure and when, and to collect their results.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines three YANG modules (common, control, report) based on the LMAP Information Model: the control module is used by a Controller to configure agents, and the report module lets agents send results to a Collector.
tldr.outcome: Agents, Controllers and Collectors from different sources can share one data model carried over protocols such as NETCONF or RESTCONF.

today: RFC 8194 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2017. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction and Terminology
sections.content:
RFC 8194 defines a data model for Large-Scale Measurement Platforms (LMAPs), described in RFC 7594. It is written in the YANG data modeling language (RFC 7950) and is based on the LMAP Information Model in RFC 8193.

The document uses a compact tree notation. Brackets enclose list keys, rw means configuration and ro means read-only state, w means RPC input, and a question mark marks an optional node, an exclamation mark a presence container, and an asterisk a list or leaf-list.
sections.eli5: This is a rulebook, written in a language computers can read, for how to set up and talk to gadgets that measure the Internet.

sections.title: The Three Modules
sections.content:
The LMAP framework has three elements. Measurement Agents (MAs) run the Measurement Tasks. A Controller tells one or more MAs which Tasks to perform and when. A Collector accepts Reports with the results.

The model is split into three modules. ietf-lmap-common.yang holds shared definitions such as data types. ietf-lmap-control.yang defines what passes between a Controller and agents. ietf-lmap-report.yang defines what passes between agents and a Collector. The Controller is the client and the MA the server for the control module; for reporting, the MA is the client and the Collector the server.
sections.eli5: There are three roles: a boss who gives out jobs, workers who do the measuring, and a collector who gathers their results. Each pair talks using its own part of the rulebook.

sections.title: The Control Data Model
sections.content:
Under the top-level lmap container the control module has five subtrees. capabilities (read-only) lists the agent's version and supported Tasks. agent holds identity and behavior: agent-id, group-id, measurement-point, flags that say whether to report each of them, controller-timeout and last-started. tasks configures the Tasks that can be invoked, each with a name, functions, an optional program, options and tags.

schedules says which Tasks run. A Schedule has a start event, an optional stop (an end event or a duration in seconds), an execution-mode and a list of Actions. Each Action names a Task and may carry options, destinations and tags, plus read-only counters such as invocations, suppressions, overlaps and failures. suppressions temporarily disable matching Schedules or Actions, and events define the triggers.
sections.eli5: The control form has boxes for who the gadget is, what jobs it knows, a timetable of when to do them, and when to stay quiet.

sections.title: Schedules, Events and Suppression
sections.content:
The execution-mode of a Schedule can be sequential, parallel or pipelined (the default). In pipelined mode, output of one Action is passed as input to the next. A Schedule's read-only state is enabled, disabled, running or suppressed.

An event is what starts or ends a Schedule. Its type is one of periodic (an interval), calendar (month, day, hour, minute, second and timezone offset), one-off, immediate, startup, controller-lost or controller-connected. Events can also have a random-spread and a cycle-interval.

A suppression has optional start and end events and one or more glob patterns in match that select tagged Schedules or Actions. With stop-running set, it also stops running Actions.
sections.eli5: Jobs can be done one after another, all at once, or in a chain. A job can start on a timer, a date, or when the boss goes missing, and a quiet-time rule can pause matching jobs.

sections.title: The Report Data Model
sections.content:
Reporting is a single RPC named report that the MA invokes on the Collector. Its input carries a date and optionally the agent-id, group-id and measurement-point, followed by a list of result entries.

Each result names the schedule, action and task, and repeats the options, parameters and tags. It records the triggering event, the start and optional end times, an optional cycle-number, and a mandatory status. Any conflict entries identify other schedules, actions or tasks involved. The measured data is in table entries, each with the function URIs, a list of column names, and rows of string values.
sections.eli5: A report is a filled-in table: which job ran, when it started and ended, whether it worked, and the numbers it found.

sections.title: Relationship to the Information Model
sections.content:
The RFC maps the six aspects of the LMAP Information Model of RFC 8193 onto the data model. Configuration Information lives in the /lmap/agent, /lmap/schedules and /lmap/tasks subtrees. Instruction Information lives in suppressions, schedules and tasks. Reporting Information is the report module, implemented by the Collector.

Some things are left out on purpose. Preconfiguration (bootstrapping) is outside scope. Channels are not modeled because a NETCONF server configuration model already covers them. Runtime logging is expected to use protocols that need no formal data model, such as syslog, and interface, hardware and firmware information can come from existing YANG models.
sections.eli5: The RFC says which part of the bigger plan each box in the form belongs to, and which things are left to other forms that already exist.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The modules are meant to be accessed through NETCONF or RESTCONF, whose mandatory-to-implement secure transports are SSH and TLS, with the NETCONF access control model restricting what each user can do. Writable nodes are sensitive. Unauthorized changes to schedules or events can cause unwanted load, send measurement traffic at victims, or switch measurements on or off at the wrong times.

Read access also needs control: capabilities and agent data can help select targets for attack, and the report operation could leak results. Because identifiers are set by the Controller, implementations must map them to safe identifiers, and option names and values must be passed literally to programs, with no shell expansion.
sections.eli5: Only trusted people should be allowed to change the timetable or read the results, or someone could make the gadgets misbehave.
